# Chat history cache: plan and progress

Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

## Decisions Kenneth owns (all settled 2026-10-29)

| # | Decision | Proposal | What M1/M2 add | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What the chat record holds | The exact request content as sent, per chat, thinking included (a chat is bound to one provider) | Thinking is part of the 3,500–9,000 tokens dropped at every turn start; Anthropic rejects edited history once thinking is carried (400 errors, accounts after 2026-08-31) | **decided 2026-10-29** (side session `local_97f342dd`): append-only record of every item ever sent, thinking included, pictures as blob references never inline base64. Visibility is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. See "Roles and lifetimes" below. |
| D2 | App notes in the project chat | Append where they happened, or never send them | A note is ~30 bytes. Not neutral: the guard test shows that without the note, two consecutive assistant replies merge into one message on Anthropic | **decided 2026-10-29**: notes become operator-role in-conversation messages (Anthropic in-array `role:"system"`, OpenAI `developer`), kept in the record, never cleared; one treatment for project and printer chat. Replaces the "JusPrin app note, not the person's words" user-text prefix. |
| D3 | Behaviour at the real context limit | Visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache, or a refusal with a message. No rolling trim | The 64 KiB trim never fired in any recorded request (max replayed history ~27 KB); R3 is a plain deletion plus whatever D3 picks | **decided 2026-10-29**: visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache. No rolling trim, no silent cut. The compaction is an item in the chat the person can see; the earlier items stay in the record with their lifetime cleared (fits D1), so it lands with R7, not before. |
| D4 | File-load "data, not instructions" reminder | Delete it; the standing prompt has said the same since 86f8395071; keep the injection eval case | 215 bytes at the very front; flips on every chat; the guard test fails at messages[0] because of it | **narrowed 2026-10-29**: either deleted (standing prompt already says it) or a turn-scoped operator message like a skill (cleared at the next user message on Anthropic, stays visible on OpenAI). **decided 2026-10-29: delete it.** Keep the injection eval case (live run, batched with the baselines). |
| D5 | Mid-chat model switching | Allowed within one wire format; a cross-format switch (Anthropic ↔ Responses, including JusPrin Cloud aliases served in different formats) starts a new chat or is hidden from the picker for an existing chat | Anthropic docs (preserved-thinking reference, as of 2026-09-03): a model switch never fails a request; blocks the new model cannot read are dropped unbilled, the stored history is never edited; the only cost is one cold cache, same as a thinking-level change. Cross-format is different: OpenAI reasoning items are encrypted and the record is in one provider's shape, so switching would mean re-rendering history, which D1 forbids | **decided 2026-10-29** (Kenneth, forked side session): keep same-format switching, no history edit on switch; R7 adds the cross-format check in `handle_set_chat_model` |
| D6 | Spend approval for phase 2 live batches | ~$1.20 per Opus run, far less per OpenAI run; two runs each (before/after) | | **approved 2026-10-29** for the phase 2 before/after batches on both providers; the OpenAI "before" run is M4. The prompt-case baseline and the injection eval case are extra batches: ask before running them. |
| D7 | Anthropic cache TTL: 5 min (1.25x write) or 1 hour (2x write) | Measurement question: the vase chat's 6-minute pause rewrote everything (13–21% of all cache writes in that run) | new from M2 gap 5 | **decided 2026-10-29: 5 min for now.** Revisit with phase 2 numbers (how often a chat pauses longer than 5 min). |
| D8 | `prompt_cache_key` per chat on OpenAI | Add it (project + chat id); without it all JusPrin users hash to the same machines and overflow above ~15 req/min | new from M2 gap 4; cheap, no behaviour change | **decided 2026-10-29: add it** (project + chat id); part of R8 |
| D9 | Write cost of a larger chat record | Never measured (searched git, memory, 1,055 Claude and 637 Codex sessions; every timing is for mesh/3MF saves). Closed without measuring: see M5. Constraint carried into D1: pictures stay blob references, never inline base64 in the document | gates nothing now | closed 2026-10-29 |

## Roles and lifetimes in the request (approved 2026-10-29)

Decided by Kenneth in the side session "Chat history cache handoff" (`local_97f342dd-4367-4bc5-830d-1c6d6d91db47`), relayed to this doc; his words: "ok. go with your proposal." The provider-doc citations below are that session's, not re-verified here.

**Append-only record, separate from visibility.** Each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model. A request renders that record plus the new items. No item is rewritten, dropped or re-derived; what the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. Source cited: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages doc (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`): a cleared message stays in the array but renders nothing, must be re-sent verbatim, and rebuilding or dropping it counts as an edit to an earlier message that fails the thinking check and breaks the cache.

**Three roles, assigned by who speaks, never by lifetime:**

| Role | Wire | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| Operator, standing | Anthropic top-level `system`; Responses `instructions` | Standing prompt and tools, written once per chat, never changed |
| Operator, in conversation | Anthropic in-array `role:"system"` (Opus 5.5 and 5.x, not Sonnet 5); OpenAI `developer` item | Situational instructions (skills; the file-load reminder if it survives D4) and app observations (notes: slice finished, hand setup change, calibration handover). The doc names "state changes your application observes" as a use case and distinguishes a user message (from the end user) from a system message (from the operator) |
| End user | `user` | The person's words plus what travels with them: workspace block, plate picture, file report. Kept in the record as sent (closes R4) |
| Tool results | `tool_result` / `function_call_output` | Their own channel, never promoted; the doc forbids relaying third-party content through system messages |

**Lifetimes.** Skills and the reminder clear at the next user message on Anthropic (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`, beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`). OpenAI has no clear, so they stay visible and should be kept short. Notes the model replied to stay visible on both providers. Thinking/reasoning is stored per chat and replayed.

**Behaviour changes, so evals are required.** Kenneth confirmed this changes what the model reads. Per his 2026-10-19 rule (last confirmed results are the baseline), every behaviour-changing step runs live prompt evals against a baseline. Baselines needed before any such step: OpenAI journeys (none exist) and the prompt-case set (check the last confirmed model and date). Request-body logging in the harness comes before all of it.

**Risks recorded, not resolved:**

- `clear_at` is a beta feature.
- Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result, so a note landing there needs a placement rule.
- OpenAI accumulates visible skill text (1.3–8.5 KB each); whether that changes answers is an eval question.
- Unverified whether the top-level `system` field and in-array system messages may coexist in one request (the doc implies yes).
- Unverified how the JusPrin Cloud gateway passes in-array system messages through in its Anthropic wire format. Production goes through the gateway, so check before R7.
- Corrections the side session made to its own earlier claims, so the tracker does not carry them: Anthropic does accept system messages inside `messages` on 5.x models; OpenAI's `instructions` parameter inserts a system/developer message rather than sitting above both.

## Phase 0: ground truth (done)

| Task | Session | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Measure recorded requests | `cache-measure` | done | `chat-history-measurement.md`. No full live request bodies exist anywhere (the app has no request-body logging; the harness cut stored results at 4,000 chars). 26 scripted bodies in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` plus Opus usage lines were measured. See findings below. |
| M2 Byte-prefix invariant test + provider cache rules | `cache-invariant` | done | Commit `378b3037a0` on `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5`: two hidden Catch2 cases, tag `[history-prefix]`, both codecs, fail on HEAD (10/102 assertions), main case passes with the prototype, skills case fails where predicted (reminder at front, Responses drops the skill). `cache-rules.md` in that worktree root: cited rules, 9 gaps. Run: `agent_bridge_tests "[history-prefix]"`. |

Fix: the save after a change is part of the outcome; the coordinator announces once, after the save; `fail()` throws `logic_error` on an announced record. 463 agent cases pass. 7 MCP bridge cases hang on HEAD too (pre-existing, not touched). |
| M4 Record an OpenAI (gpt-5.4-mini) three-chat baseline | `cache-harness` | session started 2026-10-29 after L0 merged; runs on the merged branch (after R1/R3a/R8, before R7) with `--request-log` | Also needs request-body logging in the harness (M1: none exists); add it first so M4 and phase 2 produce bodies, not just usage lines. |
| M5 Time the chat-document write on the main thread | — | skipped by Kenneth 2026-10-29 | No measurement exists, but no reason to expect a problem either: pictures already live in the attachment blob store (`attachments/<id>/<name>`), the document is text written once by write-then-rename after a 1.5 s debounce, and a text record of a long chat is on the order of 1 MB. Revisit only if D1 puts image bytes inline in the document. |

### M1 findings that change the plan

- **Never fired:** the 64 KiB trim. **Probably once:** the 16 KiB cut (bunny `object_analyze`, est. 17–19 KB, inference). Both are deletable without losing anything measured.
- **What actually changes at a turn start** (all inference on the split, no bodies): workspace blocks on each live result (1.0–1.7 KB each, ~60% of in-turn result bytes) and on the person's message; fired skill text (1.3–8.5 KB); the plate picture (~1,050 Anthropic tokens); thinking; the reminder flip; the note.
- **Cost of retelling:** turn-start rewrites were 24% of all cache-write tokens in the baseline run, 3% with the prototype.
- **Two new leak candidates (not in the handoff):**
  - Skill text sits after the moving cache breakpoint, so it is billed uncached and written one request late (2,537 tokens per file-load turn, 441 per setup turn). Fix is a breakpoint placement, independent of the reverts.
  - `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` adds `object_import` only when the request has an importable attachment. On Anthropic tools come first, so a change there voids the whole cache. Not measured; needs a check.
- **Tokens per byte:** 2.7–3.4 bytes/token on this content, not 4; byte estimates understate tokens by 15–35%.

## R2 design point from the R8 breakpoint analysis (settled: see the end of this section)

Anthropic's `clear_at: "next_user_message"` clears at the next `role:"user"` message, and a message that carries only `tool_result` blocks counts. So under R2 a skill is visible only on the request that fired it, not for the rest of the turn. That matches today's Responses codec (which drops the skill from the next request) and not today's Anthropic codec (which keeps it visible for the turn). If "cleared at the next user message" was meant as the next message from the person, `clear_at` does not do that. **My call (2026-10-29, not Kenneth's; he can override):** a skill is visible only on the request that fired it, on both providers. Reasons: it is what the OpenAI path does today and what the prompt evals were run against; `clear_at` gives it for free; the alternative needs skills kept in the record for the whole chat, which the lifetime design exists to avoid. R2 implements this; the Anthropic path loses rest-of-turn visibility, which the evals after R2 will show if it matters. Also: `cache_control` is a 400 on a turn-scoped message, so breakpoint 3 (last block of the newest user message) stays where it is; the skill-text leak then disappears on its own because a cleared message costs no input tokens and is never written to the cache. Numbers: 15 of 26 recorded bodies have skill text after the breakpoint, 81,950 bytes in total.

117	## R2 design point from the R8 breakpoint analysis (settled: see the end of this section)
118	
119	Anthropic's `clear_at: "next_user_message"` clears at the next `role:"user"` message, and a message that carries only `tool_result` blocks counts. So under R2 a skill is visible only on the request that fired it, not for the rest of the turn. That matches today's Responses codec (which drops the skill from the next request) and not today's Anthropic codec (which keeps it visible for the turn). If "cleared at the next user message" was meant as the next message from the person, `clear_at` does not do that. **My call (2026-10-29, not Kenneth's; he can override):** a skill is visible only on the request that fired it, on both providers. Reasons: it is what the OpenAI path does today and what the prompt evals were run against; `clear_at` gives it for free; the alternative needs skills kept in the record for the whole chat, which the lifetime design exists to avoid. R2 implements this; the Anthropic path loses rest-of-turn visibility, which the evals after R2 will show if it matters. Also: `cache_control` is a 400 on a turn-scoped message, so breakpoint 3 (last block of the newest user message) stays where it is; the skill-text leak then disappears on its own because a cleared message costs no input tokens and is never written to the cache. """A local stand-in for OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages streaming, to
prove the harness's --plan-journey mode without a paid call.

Each turn: the first request after the person's message gets one
workspace_inspect call, the request carrying its result gets a short text
reply. A request without tools (the chat title) gets a title. Usage is
made up from the body size so the usage listener has numbers to print.

usage: python3 -I fake_provider.py PORT LOGFILE
"""
import json
import sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

PORT = int(sys.argv[1])
LOG = open(sys.argv[2], "a", buffering=1)


def sse(events):
    out = []
    for event in events:
        out.append(f"event: {event['type']}\ndata: {json.dumps(event)}\n\n")
    return "".join(out).encode()


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length))
        size = length // 4
        if "messages" in body:
            payload, kind = self.anthropic(body, size)
        else:
            payload, kind = self.responses(body, size)
        LOG.write(f"{self.path} bytes={length} reply={kind}\n")
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(payload)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(payload)

    def responses(self, body, size):
        items = body.get("input", [])
        last = items[-1] if items else {}
        if not body.get("tools"):
            output = [{"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "Fake title"}]}]
            kind = "title"
        elif last.get("type") == "function_call_output":
            output = [{"type": "message", "role": "assistant",
                       "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "Fake reply after the inspection."}]}]
            kind = "text"
        else:
            calls = sum(1 for item in items if item.get("type") == "function_call")
            output = [{"type": "function_call", "call_id": f"call_fake_{calls + 1}", "name": "workspace_inspect",
                       "arguments": "{}"}]
            kind = "call"
        events = []
        for item in output:
            if item["type"] == "message":
                events.append({"type": "response.output_text.delta", "delta": item["content"][0]["text"]})
        usage = {"input_tokens": size, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": size // 2},
                 "output_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": size + 10}
        events.append({"type": "response.completed", "response": {"output": output, "usage": usage}})
        return sse(events), kind

    def anthropic(self, body, size):
        messages = body.get("messages", [])
        last = messages[-1] if messages else {}
        content = last.get("content", [])
        tool_result = isinstance(content, list) and any(
            isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "tool_result" for block in content)
        start = {"type": "message_start",
                 "message": {"usage": {"input_tokens": size // 4, "cache_read_input_tokens": size // 2,
                                       "cache_creation_input_tokens": size // 4, "output_tokens": 1}}}
        events = [start]
        if not body.get("tools") or tool_result:
            text = "Fake title" if not body.get("tools") else "Fake reply after the inspection."
            events += [{"type": "content_block_start", "index": 0, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}},
                       {"type": "content_block_delta", "index": 0, "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": text}},
                       {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": 0},
                       {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "end_turn"}, "usage": {"output_tokens": 10}},
                       {"type": "message_stop"}]
            kind = "title" if not body.get("tools") else "text"
        else:
            calls = sum(1 for message in messages if isinstance(message.get("content"), list)
                        for block in message["content"] if isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "tool_use")
            events += [{"type": "content_block_start", "index": 0,
                        "content_block": {"type": "tool_use", "id": f"toolu_fake_{calls + 1}", "name": "workspace_inspect",
                                          "input": {}}},
                       {"type": "content_block_delta", "index": 0, "delta": {"type": "input_json_delta", "partial_json": "{}"}},
                       {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": 0},
                       {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "tool_use"}, "usage": {"output_tokens": 10}},
                       {"type": "message_stop"}]
            kind = "call"
        return sse(events), kind


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), Handler).serve_forever()

# Harness fixes and the M4 OpenAI baseline

Session `cache-harness`, 2026-10-29. Branch `claude/cache-harness-m4-d222dd`, cut from `claude/chat-history-cache` at `0807d77282`. Untracked working doc: do not commit.

Four commits, unpushed and unmerged:

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `4d663df65c` | Stop expecting the print-issues skill on six prompt-recorder points |
| `8706ff616a` | Record the prompt suite's requests again on the cache branch |
| `d515b36d8d` | Add the three-chat journey mode to the shell harness, logged, on both providers |
| (no commit) | M4: one live OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini` run, stored in `m4-openai-baseline/` (untracked) |

Only `tests/` changed. The agent suite passes on this branch: `agent_bridge_tests --order rand`, 470 test cases, 16,415 assertions. `tests/project_prompt`'s Python tests pass (`test_steps`, `test_prefix_check`, `test_claude_cli`: 63 tests).

## 1. The scripted `direct` failure was a deliberate change; the script was stale

**Problem.** The scripted recorder run (`--project-prompt-requests`, no model) failed on more than `direct`. On the whole script it failed 12 checks: `_ends_with_print-issues` and `_sent_once_0` for six points, all on the two-plate fixture and all sending a typed message: `advice-infill`, `reply-in-german`, `troubleshoot-first-layer`, `answer-from-context`, `loaded-vs-configured`, `direct-change`. The L0 session had run only `direct`, so it saw two of them. Log: `m4-openai-baseline/evidence/step1-before-fix-harness.log`.

**Cause.** The print-issues skill is added to the first request after a plate gets slice warnings the model hasn't seen (`AgentHost::fire_print_issues`, which reads `plates[].slice_warnings` in the workspace snapshot), or after a press on a print-issue chip. The fixture's sliced plate (Bambu PLA Basic, X1 Carbon) has exactly one slice warning: OrcaSlicer's bed-temperature warning. `434e893a6b` ("Show the same slice warnings on the issue chip, to the agent and in Check print", 2026-10-28, on `jusprin-newui`) made the chip, and with it the workspace block, show only the warnings OrcaSlicer's send dialog shows. `Workspace/SliceResultWarnings.cpp` marks `BED_TEMP_TOO_HIGH_THAN_FILAMENT` as `Never`, and the commit message names this exact warning as the one it meant to drop ("which OrcaSlicer raises on every PLA print and never shows in its own window"). So the six points no longer get the skill. That is intended. The script's expectation was stale, not the code.

**Evidence.**
- The old recording (2026-10-25/26) has `sliceWarnings` with "The current hot bed temperature is relatively high…" in all six bodies. A fresh run has no `sliceWarnings` and no skill in any of them. The chip-press points (`issue-fix`, `issue-explain`) and the overhang fixture's `slice-warnings-ready` still carry the skill.
- The L0 harness binary at `282342b918` (this branch before R1 and R8) passes the fixed script with 0 failures. So the cache-programme commits (R1, R3a, R8, L0) didn't cause the failure; it came with the base `953eddb355`.
- Not done: I didn't build the parent of `434e893a6b` to bisect. The code path and the two recordings make the cause direct, and another full build was not worth it.

**Fix.** The six points lose `"skill": "print-issues"`. The README paragraph that explained why they were marked now says why the mark went. The prompt-case batches in `baseline.json` for these six were run with the skill on the request, so the next prompt-case batch is the first one without it for those six.

## 2. `requests.json` recorded again

The committed file was a Windows recording from 2026-10-25, with four skill texts copied in from macOS on 10-26. The new file is a whole macOS recording from this branch. I compared the two with `evidence/compare_recordings.py`. It normalises the known run-to-run noise: ISO timestamps, the harness's temp directory and project id, and `view_render` PNG bytes. It also parses `<workspace>` blocks and JSON tool results, so a change shows up as a JSON path. The outputs are in `evidence/step2-*.txt`.

**The three expected changes, all present:**
- `file-note-not-instructions`: the reminder item at `input[0]` is gone (R1, `e8043e2d7d`). The body now opens with the file-load report: 4 → 3 items.
- `model-imported-by-tool`: no tool list of its own any more. Every request now offers `object_import` (R8, `23cfa48bd1`), so its tools equal `project_tools.json`, and the recorder leaves them out as it does for every other point.
- The six points from step 1 have no `sliceWarnings` and no print-issues skill (`once` 1 → none). Later points on the same fixture (`after-*`, `direct-change-applied`/`-failed`, `first-person`) also lose the warning from their workspace blocks and results.

**Other changes, and why:**
- Skill wording from 2026-10-28: the print-issues skill says "pressed Ask AI" (`issue-fix`, `issue-explain`, `slice-warnings-ready`; `434e893a6b`). The setup skill in `after-intent` has the new text about the setup card's mark (`c7e62ba4f8`).
- Windows differences gone: Windows file paths, `fitsSelectedBed` false → true on the file-load points (a Windows-only fit-check bug, per the README), and OrcaSlicer's English catalog wording in the slice refusal ("not suggested for use printing filament").
- Slice figures (grams, cost, print time) differ slightly in the fourth or fifth digit.
- Revision numbers are about 10% lower throughout, and so are the handles that embed them (`f118-…` → `f106-…`); `calibration-symptom`'s object ids are shifted. **Not attributed to a commit.** Against the L0-harness recording from today they are identical, so they come from the Windows recording or from `jusprin-newui` commits between 10-25 and 10-28. I didn't separate the two.
- R3a (`a26e25bd47`, 16 KiB result cut removed) changes no body: the largest replayed result in any recording is 10,440 bytes.

**Branch-only diff.** Against a recording made by the L0 harness (`282342b918`) with the same fixed script, only three cases differ: the two R1/R8 items above, and `after-slice`'s recorded answers (next point).

**Recorder noise worth knowing.** In `after-slice`, each recorded `slice_report` answer is either a full report or `valid:false`, depending on whether the scripted slice finished before the answer was taken. Two runs of the same build differ this way, and so does the L0 harness. It affects answers only, not request bodies. Not fixed (out of scope).

**With and without `--request-log`.** The two files are **not byte-identical**, and neither are any two runs: stored tool results carry `updatedAt` timestamps and temp paths. After normalisation the run with `--request-log` equals the run without it, with no case differing (`step2-without-vs-with-request-log.txt`). Two runs without the flag differ only in the `after-slice` answers noise (`step2-run-vs-run.txt`). The committed file is the run without the flag. `baseline.json` is untouched. `test_steps.py` changed in two places: its list of points that send something once loses the six, and one comment no longer mentions the bed-temperature warning.

Note: `test_steps.py` needs the `tool_call_check` binary built (`--target tool_call_check`). Without it, 29 of its 50 tests fail on the unchanged branch.

## 3. Journey mode ported, on both providers, with request logging

`--plan-journey <model-file> <exchange-directory>` is ported from the uncommitted diff in `opus-cost-batch`. The turn loop and the `turn-N.json` writer are unchanged. Nothing from that worktree's `src/` was ported. What changed from that diff:

- The Agent is built the way the app builds one for a saved key: `make_provider_agent` with the provider row's codec and the app's HTTP transport, for both providers. `JUSPRIN_JOURNEY_PROVIDER` = `openai` (the default, with `OPENAI_API_KEY`) or `anthropic` (with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). `JUSPRIN_JOURNEY_MODEL` sets the model; `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` sets the endpoint.
- The old OpenAI path went through an OpenRouter host-pinning transport that also stripped every picture. I dropped it, because a cost baseline has to send what the app sends.
- `--request-log` works in this mode. The transport and agent are wrapped with `RequestLog` as `install_harness_agent` does for the other modes, and the log records the right provider id.
- The usage line has one shape on both providers and always includes `cache_creation_tokens` (0 on OpenAI).

**How it was verified, with no paid call:** I ran a local fake provider (`evidence/fake_provider.py`) that streams OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages events: one `workspace_inspect` call, then a text reply, per turn. I ran one OpenAI journey (vase) and one Anthropic journey (plug), each a file load plus one message, then `END`. Each produced 5 requests (two per turn plus the chat title), all logged with the right provider and URL and with usage. Both got HARNESS RESULT PASS, and `prefix_check.py` reads both logs. `--request-log` with an unsupported mode (`--mcp`) still exits 2. The fake runs are in `evidence/fake-journeys/`.

## 4. M4: OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini` three-chat baseline (one approved run)

I used the same three chats as the Opus baseline (`opus-batch/out-baseline/`).
